newsitem.title: USA: NASD adopts plan for to cut minimum quote steps.
newsitem.headline: NASD adopts plan for to cut minimum quote steps.

text.p: The National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD) said Thursday it approved a proposal to narrow the quotation increments for securities traded on Nasdaq whose bid is $10 per share or more.

The NASD proposal calls for the increments to be cut to 1/16th of a dollar (6.25 cents) from 1/8th of a dollar (12.5 cents). Stocks under $10 are already quoted in increments of 1/16ths, the trade group said in a statement.
The proposal must now be approved by the Securities and Exchange Commission before it can become effective and would begin within one month after receiving SEC approval.

The proposal approval comes on the heels of legislation introuced by lawmakers last month that would require the SEC to develop a plan within a year to transition stock and options markets away from trading in fractions.
The proposed NASD change would "enhance market transparency and allow investors a greater opportunity to obtain better prices," the trade group said in a statement.
The move could servce as a substitute for the rounding indicator required under the SEC Order Handling Rules.

The SEC granted Nasdaq, the exchanges and market participants such as market-making firms, an extension to the rounder indicator requirement until July 31, 1997 due to the large number of system modifications it would require.
NASD is a trade group for the U.S. financial industry and a self-regulatory organization under SEC oversight. NASD runs Nasdaq stock market as a separate unit.
